items.h: Art Basel Hong Kong publishes its 2027 exhibitor list for 25–27 March
items.s: Galleries, Discoveries, Insights and Echoes sectors at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre; the list went up on 24 November, ArtAsiaPacific reports.

items.h: Elie Khouri’s foundation to open in Dubai in late 2028, led by Christie’s former Middle East head
items.s: The Elie Khouri Art Foundation (founded 2021; works by more than 300 artists) will occupy a coastal villa in Jumeirah 1 redesigned by Sumayya Vally’s Counterspace. Caroline Louca, formerly managing director of Christie’s Middle East, will direct it.

items.h: Kalshi’s 58 New York lot markets traded about $636,000; the crowd overshot the Van Gogh and the Basquiat
items.s: 7,127 trades at $1 contract value; the Van Gogh drew $97,886. Traders gave a 58% chance of clearing $200m; it made $190.4m. They gave 80% to the Basquiat beating $35m; it made $32.9m. Artnet counts 64.2% of the seven evening sales’ estimated value as guaranteed.

items.h: New York’s November week makes about $2.44bn, up from $2.23bn last year
items.s: Evening sales about $2.03bn against a $1.7bn combined low estimate. Sotheby’s $1.2bn in evening sales, up 18%; Christie’s $772m, down 5%; Phillips $104.4m, up 55%.

items.h: Christie’s 21st Century sale makes $145.9m, below its $126–192m estimate at hammer
items.s: Hammer $117.7m. The Basquiat sold for $32.8m ($28m hammer) under its $30–50m estimate; about 59% of lots were guaranteed and a Marian Goodman Richter failed at $5.7m.

items.h: Nara’s In the Milky Lake / Thinking One makes $15.9m at Fair Warning
items.s: Four bidders, an American buyer; just over the $15m high estimate and his third-highest price.

items.h: Twenty artist records in New York, from Van Gogh to Julia Jo
items.s: Records for Van Gogh, Kandinsky, Sam Francis, Kusama, Aaron Douglas, Cornelis van Haarlem ($13.9m) and Wifredo Lam ($11.6m), among others.

items.h: Bonhams’s five Brâncuși bronzes reported sold for about $15.1m, under a $25m estimate
items.s: All five posthumous casts; Bonhams has published no result.

items.h: Hilma af Klint’s Ser III No. 5 makes SEK 128.9m, a Nordic auction record
items.s: About $12.7m (Hyperallergic) against SEK 6–8m; hammer SEK 108m. Her previous record was $165,825.

items.h: Frieze Abu Dhabi opens at Manarat Al Saadiyat with about 88 galleries
items.s: Preview 19 November, closing 22 November; Abu Dhabi Art’s last edition had 142.

items.h: Van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs sells for a record $190.4m as Sotheby’s night makes $777.8m
items.s: The guaranteed Van Gogh hammered at $165m, below its guide, to William Acquavella in the room. The Blaquier-Arrieta collection made $412m against about $450m; the Modern sale $365.8m, within estimate.

items.h: Modigliani’s limestone Tête makes $44.6m at Phillips after a three-way contest
items.s: Phillips’s evening sale made $104.4m ($85.75m hammer), up 55% on last year; 20 of 21 lots sold and 14 of 22 were guaranteed.

items.h: Kandinsky’s Betonte Ecken sets a $85.8m record as Christie’s 20th Century sale makes $626.6m
items.s: Hammer $521m, at the low end of a $511–743m estimate. The Klimt made $82.3m; the Koons collection’s Le Baiser $31.1m, below its estimate. Kahlo, Calder and Stella were withdrawn.

items.h: Sotheby’s settles with the Fischer heirs hours before the $180m Van Gogh sale
items.s: An agreement between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and all the Fischers’ legal descendants; the terms are not public. The lot stayed in the sale.

items.h: Kusama sets a $15m record as Sotheby’s opens New York with $378.7m
items.s: The Baum collection made $109.9m, all 24 lots sold; The Now and Contemporary made $268.7m, its $224.78m hammer just under the low estimate.

items.h: Phillips steps back from the top end: “time really to look at profitability”
items.s: Chief executive Martin Wilson says Phillips no longer aims to grow at all costs. Its two top lots this week are estimated above $10m, against 45 such lots at Christie’s and Sotheby’s together. A syndicated report.

items.h: Fischer heirs challenge Sotheby’s $180m Van Gogh days before the Blaquier-Arrieta sale
items.s: The heirs say Châtaigniers en fleurs was sold under duress in 1936. Sotheby’s says its research has not established that and that it is working towards a resolution. The lot is guaranteed.

items.h: Heirs’ lawyer: “no auction may take place” unless Sotheby’s proves the 1936 Van Gogh sale was fair
items.s: Gunnar Schnabel wrote to Sotheby’s on 12 November; the heirs cite the Reich flight tax the family paid. They say they will seek a solution under the 1998 Washington Principles.

items.h: Shanghai art week finds buyers in a more selective market
items.s: West Bund (85 galleries) and Art021 (111) opened as speculative buyers left. Reported sales include a Megan Rooney at £400,000 (Ropac) and a Louise Bourgeois at $450,000 to a Kuala Lumpur museum (Hauser & Wirth).

items.h: Hedreen collection goes to Sotheby’s to repay a loan, not to fund a museum
items.s: About 50 works, at least $109–158m, led by a Lichtenstein and a de Kooning at $20–30m each. The collection had been pledged to Seattle University’s planned museum.

items.h: Bonhams shows five Brâncuși bronzes, about $25m, before Brancusi: The Legacy on 18 November
items.s: The bronzes are on view at the new flagship at 111 West 57th Street.

items.h: New York’s four houses expect $2.04–2.4bn this week
items.s: Sotheby’s more than $1.1bn, a house record for a marquee season; Christie’s $823m–1.1bn; Phillips $80.4–128.7m; Bonhams at least $40m.

items.h: Art Basel cuts stand fees by 20% for all 211 Art Basel Paris exhibitors after the early closure
items.s: The fair, closed two days early by rioting, ran about three and a half of its five and a half days. The galleries’ committee, the CPGA, had accused the organiser of “disrespect, even contempt”; its president says 20% is what it expected. Noah Horowitz stands by the closure.

items.h: Artnet becomes Kalshi’s art partner: prediction markets on the New York sales are already trading
items.s: Yes-or-no contracts on auction and fair outcomes, settled on Artnet’s Price Database; markets on Miami Art Week follow later in November.

items.h: Collector Elie Khouri to open a home for his foundation in Dubai in 2028
items.s: A Jumeirah villa redesigned by Counterspace will house the Elie Khouri Art Foundation; the collection spans more than 300 artists, with Middle Eastern art at its core.

items.h: Shanghai art week opens with West Bund and Art021 under a slower economy
items.s: West Bund Art & Design runs 10–15 November and Art021 11–14 November. Dealers describe a market still growing, but much more slowly, after the property crash and deflation.

items.h: Five lost Rubens sketches reunited in Gotha after 80 years
items.s: The Prophet Elijah came back from a private American collection in a settlement mediated by Cabinet Turquin and paid for by the Ernst von Siemens Art Foundation, at a reported “figure in the low millions”, below market price.

items.h: Paris court orders the Pissarro sold at Sotheby’s London for £1.2m returned to the Flavian heirs
items.s: The court voided the 2024 sale, found the painting looted in 1941 and gave Sotheby’s two months to name the buyer; claims against Sotheby’s were dismissed. Mondex intends to appeal.

items.h: US tariffs of 50% hit Canadian galleries
items.s: In force since 22 August on Canadian paintings, sculpture and prints. Equinox Gallery expects its US buyers, about 15% of sales, to fall to zero; Macaulay & Co has dropped a Miami Art Week fair.

items.h: French prosecutors investigate Picasso heirs’ fraud claim over plates and medallions
items.s: An Aix-en-Provence investigation into Ateliers Hugo silver plates and gold medallions; a set of 24 plates made £1.4m at Sotheby’s London in 2021. The Picasso Administration counts at least 17 suspect collections.

items.h: Sotheby’s to offer a newly discovered Altdorfer landscape at £3–5m
items.s: A landscape of about 1520 from a Swiss private collection leads Sotheby’s Old Masters Evening Sale in London on 9 December. It is one of three known oil landscapes by Altdorfer; it is on view in New York from 7 to 19 November.

items.h: Guillaume Cerutti, formerly Christie’s chief executive, named president of Versailles
items.s: Cerutti, 60, succeeds Christophe Leribault, who moved to the Louvre in February. He led the Pinault Collection from January 2025 to March 2026.

items.h: Four Vienna galleries close or leave amid a tougher market
items.s: Exile and Zeller van Almsick are closing, Layr is moving to a project-based model, and Eva Presenhuber is leaving Vienna. Rising costs and an unpredictable market are blamed.

items.h: Christie’s Paris offers a Fragonard head unseen for a century at €400,000–600,000
items.s: Tête de jeune femme by Jean-Honoré Fragonard was offered in Paris on 4 November.

items.h: New York’s November sales: a Van Gogh and a Cézanne near the $100m mark
items.s: Sotheby’s Blaquier-Arrieta collection, valued at nearly $450m, puts the Van Gogh at about $180m and the Cézanne at about $120m on 18 November.

items.h: ArtTactic: contemporary confidence up to 56 from 43 in March
items.s: Auction-market confidence rose to 78 from 69 and primary-market confidence to 51 from 45. Sixty per cent of experts expect flat sales over six months, and the two previous rallies faded within half a year.

items.h: Italy moves to create a restitution panel for Nazi-looted art
items.s: A bill before the lower house’s culture committee would set up a five-member committee to rule on claims for art lost from 1933 to 1945, within 180 days of a claim.

items.h: Christie’s first Abu Dhabi auction makes $8.9m with nine records
items.s: MAWASIM made $8.94m with premium. Three of the nine records were artist records, two were for a medium and four were auction debuts. Thirty-seven per cent of registrants were new to Christie’s.
